'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**[[Jihadist insurgency in Burkina Faso]]
***[[Siege of Djibo]]
****At least 28 people are killed, including ten [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces|soldiers]], and at least 50 others are injured, after gunmen attack a [[military base]] in [[Djibo]], [[Burkina Faso]]. Eighteen attackers are killed in the ensuing gunfight. [https://www.panapress.com/28-dead-including-10-Burkinabe-s-a_630733421-lang2.html (Panapress)] [https://news.yahoo.com/ten-soldiers-killed-50-wounded-173330816.html (Reuters via Yahoo! News)]
*[[Internal conflict in Myanmar]]
**[[Kachin conflict]]
***[[Hpakant massacre]]
****At least 50 people are killed and at least 100 others are injured when the [[Tatmadaw|military]] launches [[airstrike]]s at a concert in [[Kachin State]] celebrating the 62nd anniversary of the founding of the [[separatist]] [[Kachin Independence Army]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-63370732 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 south eastern Australia floods]]
**The body of a woman is found on the bank of a river amid ongoing flooding in [[New South Wales]], bringing the death toll to three. [https://7news.com.au/weather/severe-weather/more-rain-to-hit-north-and-west-victoria-as-two-weather-systems-strike-new-south-wales-c-8638276 (7 News)]
*Thirteen people are killed, several others are injured, and an unknown number of people are reported missing after a passenger ship catches fire off the coast of [[East Nusa Tenggara]], [[Indonesia]]. 263 passengers have been rescued. [https://english.news.cn/asiapacific/20221024/c3b225fef5a04511ad6225464c30ab63/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Mass shootings in the United States]]
**[[2022 Central Visual and Performing Arts High School shooting]]
***Two people are killed and eight others are injured during a [[mass shooting]] at the [[Central Visual and Performing Arts High School]] in [[St. Louis]], [[Missouri]]. The perpetrator is killed by police. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/oct/24/st-louis-school-shooting-latest (''The Guardian'')]
**Aftermath of the [[2021 Oxford High School shooting]]
***Ethan Crumbley pleads guilty to four counts of [[murder (United States law)|murder]], seven counts of [[attempted murder]], 12 counts of use of a firearm in the commission of a felony, and one count of terrorism. [https://www.fox2detroit.com/news/ethan-crumbley-accused-oxford-school-mass-shooter-pleads-guilty-to-murder-terrorism (WJBK-TV)] 
*It is reported that the email server of the [[Atomic Energy Organization of Iran]]'s Nuclear Power Production and Development company was hacked, with a number of emails being leaked. [https://www.tasnimnews.com/en/news/2022/10/23/2792545/aeoi-dismisses-media-hype-on-cyberattack (Tasnim)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[October 2022 Conservative Party leadership election]], [[October 2022 United Kingdom government crisis]]
**[[Rishi Sunak]] is selected as the [[Leader of the Conservative Party (UK)|Leader of the Conservative Party]] and will become the next [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]] after [[Penny Mordaunt]] withdrew her bid. [https://news.stv.tv/politics/rishi-sunak-set-to-be-next-uk-prime-minister-after-winning-leadership-contest (STV News)]
*[[October 2022 votes of no confidence in the government of Élisabeth Borne]]
**The [[Borne government|French government]] survives three motions of no confidence tabled by the left-wing and right-wing opposition. [https://www.tf1info.fr/politique/motions-de-censure-nupes-rn-article-49-3-pourquoi-l-opposition-ne-renversera-pas-le-gouvernement-elisabeth-borne-2236071.html (TF1)]
'''Science and technology'''
*In a landmark finding affecting [[contact sport]]s, the [[United States]] [[National Institutes of Health]] formally acknowledge a causal link between repeated blows to the head and the [[neurodegenerative disease]] [[chronic traumatic encephalopathy|CTE]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2022/oct/24/us-health-body-rules-collision-sports-cause-cte-in-landmark-change (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[Vrak – Museum of Wrecks|Swedish Museum of Wrecks]] announces that [[Maritime archaeology|maritime archaeologists]] have discovered the [[shipwreck|wreck]] of the 17th-century warship ''Äpplet'', believed to be the sister ship of [[Vasa (ship)|''Vasa'']], which sank off the island of [[Vaxholm]] near [[Stockholm]] in 1629. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/oct/24/lost-17th-century-warship-found-in-sweden (''The Guardian'')]
